bullets: Game 8 of 8 in a single-deck video ('#1 BEST Ronin Deck in Clash Royale'), video time 1358.5-1573.9s, against Graveyard control with the Hero Tombstone. Ryley wins it in double-elixir overtime on his own call: "That's going to line up on the knight and that's game. That's tower. Is it not? Let's go. Good game" (1564-1566s).

Two of the eight slots are variants: the Goblin Barrel is the evolution ("Let's go for the evo barrel here", 1470s) and the Magic Archer is the Hero - he calls for a "step back" and for the arrows to "line up" at 1420s, 1542s, 1552s and 1561-1565s, and three unattributed own 2-elixir drops (t=1488.0, 1550.2, 1563.1) match Triple Threat.

Piloting rule stated at 1404-1406s: "I need to be really aggressive in this match if I want to have a chance." In practice every defensive rotation is followed within seconds by a threat in the other lane - Cannon + Skeletons at clock 2:18 into Fire Spirit at the bridge at 2:05; Magic Archer + Cannon + Skeletons at 0:43 into Wall Breakers and Goblin Barrel at 0:32.

The two cheap win conditions are deliberately stacked so one spell cannot answer both: "Let's barrel wall breakers again. Keep up the pressure" (1500-1503s), "let's go for the barrel plus wall breakers here" (1515-1518s), "let's spirit barrel here then we wall breakers opposite lane. I think he's just cooked" (1533-1537s).

The Ronin is the deck's one heavy commitment and Ryley plays it three ways in this game - behind the tower as a build-up at clock 2:37, deep on his own half as defence at 1:52 and 1:27, and as a straight bridge run at 1:03 and in overtime. Its stated liability against a Tornado deck: "I think you can activate king tower off the Ronin, so I'm hoping he doesn't have [Tornado]... cuz that would be really bad" (1375-1381s), which the opponent immediately executes at 1382s.

The list has no spell, so buildings and spawners get solved by threat instead of removal: against the Hero Tombstone he refuses to spend and forces the commitment - "Not going to fire spirit for the tombstone. I'm just going to wait for him to tombstone and then can threaten a magic archer on top of that knight cuz he has to be really careful" (1518-1525s).

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers, Skeletons and two spirits all bait the same small spells, and at 2.5 average elixir he re-presents them faster than a single answer can cover both lanes.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Three separate win conditions (Ronin, Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers) plus five one-to-three elixir cards mean the opponent has to hold an answer for each while Ryley cycles back to them roughly every rotation. The deck carries no spell at all, so it solves buildings and spawners by threatening around them instead of removing them - against the opponent's Hero Tombstone he simply refuses to spend and waits: "Not going to fire spirit for the tombstone. I'm just going to wait for him to tombstone and then can threaten a magic archer on top of that knight" (1518-1524s). Defence is a Cannon plus Skeletons or a spirit, and the Hero Magic Archer covers the deck's two real problems - Graveyard and air - with Triple Threat used both to dodge Poison and to aim the triple shot. Its clear weakness is Tornado: the Ronin can be dragged into the opponent's king tower and activate it, which is exactly what happens at 1382s.
